read.gkReflex: A reflex keeper ({reflex}) more than a sweeper ({one}): keep the line deep and let the shots come to the pads.
read.gkOneOnOne: Strong one-on-one ({one}) — push the line up, the keeper closes the space behind it.
read.gkBalanced: A balanced keeper (reflexes {reflex}, one-on-one {one}). Shape the defence around the backs, not the keeper.
read.fwdBaseline: Quickest first three metres in the squad and comfortable receiving on the reverse — a baseline-entry forward, not a target man. Long-ball build-up wastes that: {goals} goals so far, the flank entry with a trailing runner is the pattern.
read.fwdFinisher: A finisher (hit {hit}): wants the ball on the spot strip, early. Build through the middle and get the ball to the top of the D.
read.fwdWorker: A worker (work rate {work}): the first presser, the runner who makes the second line press work. Worth more in a full-court press than in a low block.
read.midPlaymaker: Sees the pass (vision {vision}) — the outlet through the middle runs through this player. Protect the minutes in the last quarter.
read.midAerial: Comfortable in the air ({aerial}): the direct outlet over a press. On watered turf the flat ball is faster, so use it when pressed, not by default.
read.midEngine: An engine (work rate {work}, stamina {stamina}): rotates late, covers the press. Rotate below 55 % and this player plays all four quarters.
read.defFlicker: A drag flick of {flick} — the PC battery's striker. Protect the player from green cards: the battery without the flicker is a lost corner.
read.defStopper: A stopper (tackling {tackle}): the marker for their best runner in the D. Ask for the channel tackle, not the lunge.
read.defOutlet: An outlet defender (push {push}): plays the first pass from the 23. Width on the outlet, never the back pass into the D.

plan.disciplineInD: The corner is their weapon. Stay out of trouble in your own circle: no stick, no foot, no risk.
plan.attackEarly: Their defence leaks. Press them early and get to the circle quickly.
plan.overTheTop: They press full-court. Go over it — long ball or aerial — rather than through it.
plan.patientWide: They sit in a zone. Patience and width: switch the play and work the top of the circle.
plan.switchSides: Split press: they steer you to one side. Switch quickly to the other flank.

rules.stageHint: Click a rule to see it on the pitch — the scene loops.
rules.videoNote: opens YouTube in a new tab
rules.title: The rulebook
rules.sub: The FIH rules as they apply on the pitch — and as the game whistles them.

feet.title: Feet in the circle
feet.body: A ball that hits a defender's foot or body inside the circle is almost always a penalty corner — in the circle the advantage is close to automatic; outside it, the umpire only whistles when an advantage is gained. The attacker who plays the ball at feet is within the rules — the defender must keep the body out of the line.

dangerous.title: Dangerous play
dangerous.body: A ball raised at an opponent within five metres above knee height is dangerous play: free hit against the striker — and if a defender does it in their own circle, it becomes a penalty corner or a stroke.

backStick.title: Back-stick
backStick.body: Only the flat face of the stick may play the ball. The rounded side is a free hit.

obstruction.title: Obstruction
obstruction.body: Shielding the ball with the body, backing into an opponent or running across a player going for the ball is obstruction — a free hit.

stickTackle.title: Stick tackle
stickTackle.body: Hitting, hooking or holding an opponent's stick is a free hit; inside the circle a penalty corner.

freeHitDistance.title: Five metres at a free hit
freeHitDistance.body: Opponents must be five metres from the ball at a free hit. Standing closer — or rushing the restart — is a free hit to the other side.

selfPass23.title: Self-pass after a free hit inside the 23
selfPass23.body: The attacker may self-pass, but from a free hit inside the attacking 23 the ball must travel five metres or be touched by a defender before it enters the circle. Closing the five metres is how the defence kills it.

pcBreach.title: Breaking early at a penalty corner
pcBreach.body: Defenders behind the backline and attackers outside the circle must wait for the injection. Whoever breaks early — defender or attacker — is sent beyond the halfway line and the corner is taken again; a defender sent off the line cannot be replaced, so his side defends it a man short.

pcFirstHit.title: The first hit at a penalty corner
pcFirstHit.body: The first shot at goal at a penalty corner, if it is a hit, must cross the goal line below 460 mm. A drag flick or a push may go at any height.

stroke.title: Penalty stroke
stroke.body: A stroke is awarded for an offence that prevents a probable goal or a deliberate foul in the circle. One push or flick from 6.4 m, the keeper on the line; the taker may not take it before the whistle.

circle.title: The circle rule
circle.body: A goal counts only if the ball was touched by an attacker inside the circle before crossing the goal line. Nothing scores from outside the D — which is why the whole game lives there.

pc.title: Penalty corner
pc.body: Injected from the backline ten metres from the post; at most five defenders — keeper included — behind the line, everybody else beyond the halfway line; the ball must leave the circle before a shot unless trapped at the top. Awarded for a foul by a defender in the circle or a deliberate one inside the 23.

cards.title: Cards
cards.body: Green: two minutes off. Yellow: five or ten minutes off. Red: the rest of the match. Persistent fouling escalates.

subs.title: Rolling substitutions
subs.body: Any number of substitutions at any time through the dugout gate — except during a penalty corner, when only an injured or suspended keeper may be replaced.

aerial.title: The aerial
aerial.body: A raised ball is legal when it is safe: not towards an opponent within five metres, and received by one player with opponents five metres away until it is controlled.

about.title: About BULLY OFF
about.intro: A field-hockey coach/manager game in which every match is really played. Everything in it is fictional and everything runs on your device.
about.privacy1: No real clubs and no real people. Clubs, players, coaches and towns are generated from common-name pools and checked against a list of real clubs; no person is modelled, rated or named.
about.privacy2: No accounts, no telemetry, no analytics, no advertising. The app makes no network requests after it has loaded; your careers live in your browser's storage (IndexedDB) and in the files you export yourself.
about.privacy3: Replays and saves you export contain only generated data. Sharing them shares nothing about you.
about.privacy4: Club mode (entering your own squad) is not part of v1.0; when it comes it will be local-only and clearly marked.
about.offline: Installed as an app, BULLY OFF works without a connection: the match, the world generator and your saves are local.
about.credits: The rulebook links to explainer videos on YouTube: they open in a new tab only when you click one — nothing is embedded and nothing is loaded up front. Open source (MIT). A match model that replays every match exactly, the FIH rules, players who make their own decisions, a season model with twenty seasons of generated history, and a replay viewer — calibrated against public Belgian League aggregates.

academy.title: Academy
academy.sub: What really happens on the pitch — one topic a minute.

penaltyCorner.title: The penalty corner
penaltyCorner.sub: About a third of all goals come from here.

battery.title: The battery
battery.body: Injector, trapper, striker. The injection has to arrive at about 8 m/s: harder and the trapper cannot stop it, softer and the runner beats the ball to the spot.

variants.title: The variants
variants.body: Drag flick, low hit, slip left or right, deflection. Each variant breaks a different running-out system — and every running-out system has a hole.

runningOut.title: Running out
runningOut.body: The first runner leaves on the injection and guesses two things: his line and his height. Low blocks the hit but is flicked over; high blocks the flick but the low hit goes under him.

wearOut.title: Wearing it out
wearOut.body: Run the same variant nine times and they set up for it. Keep one back for when it matters.

buildUp.title: Building out
buildUp.sub: From your own 23 to halfway without giving it away.

shape.title: The shape
shape.body: Backs split around your own circle — never receive inside your D. A ball played back in there is a turnover with a goal attached.

freeMan.title: The free man
freeMan.body: The spare back nobody is marking is your whole outlet. Find him first, then play forward.

upBackThrough.title: Up-back-through
upBackThrough.body: Into a pressed forward, straight back to the free man, then through the line that has just come with it. This is the combination that makes a build-up look coached.

overTheTop.title: Over the top
overTheTop.body: A full-court press has no spare man. One ball over the top and you are a player up.

systems.title: The four systems
systems.body: Full court: man-to-man over the whole pitch, nobody spare. Half court: the block sets around halfway. Split: shepherd to one side and slide across. Zone: everyone behind the 23 and nobody chases.

channels.title: Who steps out
channels.body: The player whose channel the ball is in, not whoever happens to be nearest. A right half who sprints across the pitch leaves exactly the gap the ball is going to.

freeManRest.title: Free man and rest-break
freeManRest.body: A spare defender behind the line covers the mistake. Two forwards who do not come back are the reason you conceded the ball in the first place.

split.title: The splitting press
split.body: The first defender closes from the inside, the ball has to go wide, the block slides across. You concede the far side on purpose — until they find it.

circleEntry.title: Into the circle
circleEntry.sub: Nothing scores from outside the D.

theLine.title: The line
theLine.body: Possession in midfield is worth comparatively little. The pass that crosses the circle line is the most valuable object on the pitch.

baseline.title: Baseline and pull-back
baseline.body: Round the back on the outside, on to the backline, and pull it back to the spot where the runner arrives. The largest goal source in the modern game.

switchSlip.title: Switch and slip
switchSlip.body: Circulate across the top of the D until the block slides with it, then slip the ball in behind them to the far post.

drawTheFoot.title: Drawing the foot
drawTheFoot.body: A firm push at a defender standing between the ball and the goal. A foot in the circle is a corner — that is where most club-level corners come from.
